subject: Security exhibit: scoped inspection rights, pen-test carveouts, and evidence sprint plan
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@evergreenhealth.org>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@evergreenhealth.org>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security exhibit: scoped inspection rights and pen-test carveouts

Monica —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get clarity on a couple items in the MSA/order form, specifically the security exhibit (SOC 2 attachments and pen test language). Our legal team is nervous about broad inspection rights and unlimited pen-test clauses. We put together a short list (attached) with the asks:

- Confirmation of SOC 2 availability and how long Redwood retains reports
- Pen-test frequency and whether they can be run without Redwood engineering present
- Scope: can we limit to a tenant/staging environment vs. production?
- Evidence cadence: what artifacts will Redwood provide (logs, config snapshots, architecture diagram) and on what schedule

We need to turn around a redline before our vendor committee meets next Thursday. Can you share your suggested compromise language or an annotated redline?

Attached: Evergreen_Security_Questions.xlsx

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Director, Vendor Risk
Evergreen Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@evergreenhealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Security exhibit: scoped inspection rights and pen-test carveouts

Tom —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers up front and then next steps below.

1) SOC 2: We can share the latest SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA (standard). We retain reports and associated audit artifacts for 24 months; we can add a summary that is safe to share in the order form.

2) Pen testing: Redwood permits 1 customer-initiated pen test per 12 months (we can make that 1 per 12 months per order form). Tests must be scoped and scheduled with 30 days' notice and conducted in staging (customer-owned tenant or a Redwood-provisioned staging environment). Redwood engineering will be on call; any request for production access requires executive approval and is rare.

3) Scope & Access: We propose bounded inspection rights: inspection shall be limited to (a) customer-specific tenancy and (b) discrete artifacts identified in Exhibit A. No unfettered access to multi-tenant production hosts. Ephemeral credentials and a 4-hour timebox for interactive sessions is our standard operational compromise.

4) Evidence cadence: We can provide an initial evidence bundle during onboarding (SOC 2 summary, architecture diagram, sample logs), then a quarterly evidence snapshot for the first year, and on-demand artifacts tied to material change requests or requested audits (with 14 business days to produce).

Next steps — proposed:
- I've attached an initial redline (redlines_v1.docx) that reflects the bounded inspection language above and a pen-test scheduling clause.
- Ben / Karthik / Laura, can you review the draft language and mark legal items we should not concede? If okay, we can present to Tom's team and iterate.

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cRedlines (draft)

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Evergreen redlines — quick notes

Team —

Quick internal notes after skimming Monica's draft:

- Pen-test frequency: I agree with 1 per 12 months, but suggest adding an operational carveout allowing an additional test for security incidents with mutual agreement (so we can deny gratuitous tests).
- Staging access: keep it explicit that staging is customer-provided or Redwood-provisioned isolated tenant; no shared-host access.
- Evidence delivery: the quarterly snapshot is fine, but procurement will push for fixed SLAs (e.g., 10 business days to deliver logs). Recommend we propose 14 business days and add escalation path if evidence can't be produced in time.
- Liability: procurement may push to expand the pen-test wording into warranty or indemnity. Flag to legal — do not accept indemnity tied to customer testing.

I redlined 2 small operational clarifications in the draft (note attached in the Drive link). If legal is OK, I think this is customer-manageable.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:41:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Internal: Evergreen redlines — legal edits

Folks —

I reviewed redlines_v1 and made targeted legal edits. Key points to surface to customer:

1) Inspection rights must be limited to documented artifacts (Exhibit A) and tenant-level access. We will not agree to broad "inspection" of Redwood infrastructure or multi-tenant resources.

2) Pen test clause: we will agree to 1 customer-initiated test per 12 months with 30 days' notice. Any test that requires access beyond a scoped staging tenant needs written executive approval and coordination with Redwood's incident response lead. Add 4-hour interactive window cap per session; additional time requires pre-approval.

3) Notice & evidence cadence: 14 business days to deliver requested non-production artifacts; for production-facing artifacts we need to triage through our security team with agreed timelines. Add an explicit escalation path to Legal -> Security -> SOC lead if timelines slip.

4) Liability & indemnity: carve out indemnity requests tied to customer testing — we can provide a limitation of liability statement and require tests to be conducted by accredited third parties with proof of insurance.

I've attached the tracked document (security-exhibit-redline-track.docx) and a short comment list. If you want me to run this by counsel for sign-off before customer delivery, I can do that tomorrow.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts 
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@evergreenhealth.org>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@evergreenhealth.org>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Security exhibit: scoped inspection rights and pen-test carveouts

Monica/Karthik —

Thanks — that all looks reasonable and addresses most of our committee concerns. A couple quick asks from procurement:

- Can we get confirmation that SOC 2 summary + auditor contact will be provided via a secure link (not shared PDF by email)?
- For the pen test: our security team is asking for a 4-hour interactive window in staging (fine) but also wants the option for one vendor-led code-level assessment during that window. Would Redwood consider allowing vendor access limited to the customer tenant for the 4-hour timebox, provided the vendor signs Redwood's testing rules and has insurance?

If yes, we can accept the 1-per-12-month approach with the 30-day notice and produce a short statement of work for the test that we can attach to the order form. Procurement (Elena) is on this thread to coordinate timelines — we are targeting contract signature by 3/4.

Tom
Director, Vendor Risk
Evergreen Health
